items.title: Cheats in GTA 6 are weirdly restrictive, and I'm counting the minutes until the PC version fixes them
items.summary:
Using cheats in GTA 6 is a given. GTA games are big, beautiful sandboxes of destruction, and sometimes I want to forget about story missions and just magically fill my pockets with cash, spawn a tank or a jet, and go on a rampage with infinite incendiary ammo.

Naturally, you can do that with GTA 6 cheats . But only eventually. If you were hoping to try out some cheats the moment you step into the game, I've got some bad news for you—and then some worse news. Here are the problems:

You can't unlock cheats until you've completed the main story. Maybe that's fair—Rockstar devs don't want you busting out cheats and skipping through the game they spent 10 years crafting. But then again, if you shell out potentially $100 for a game, shouldn't you be able to play it however the heck you want? I think so.

GTA 6 is a big, long game, with a five chapter main story that contains 91 missions. It took me about 90 hours to finish, at which point I could finally access the cheats menu.

That's where I found the next bit of bad news...

You have to unlock cheats individually through milestones and challenges Congrats on playing those 90 hours: are you ready for 90 more? Most cheats on the menu are locked because there are requirements you need to meet to use them. Want a cheat that removes fall damage? First you'll need to survive 20 falls of over more than 40 feet. Want to spawn a parachute? First complete 50 skydives and basejumps.

Using an infinite ammo cheat means first winning 25 medals on shooting ranges. To fast-forward time you'll need to find 10 collectible watches—and in 90…

items.title: Ubisoft says Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced 'outperformed expectations,' lays off 166 more people anyway
items.summary:
Ubisoft has laid off 166 people from its offices in Montreal and Quebec City, saying in a statement provided to PC Gamer that its "production needs are changing, requiring us to adjust the size of some teams to ensure our resources are aligned with current production priorities and business needs."

Founded in 1997, Ubisoft Montreal is one of the biggest game studios in the world, with roughly 4,000 employees as of 2022. Ubisoft Quebec, launched in 2005, is somewhat smaller but still substantial: Its website says the studio has "a team of over 600 creative, passionate, and innovative talents." The cuts reportedly impact employees who could not be assigned elsewhere after their existing projects were cancelled or rescoped.

Whatever the reason, it's bleak: This is the latest round in a series of layoffs that have battered the company since it announced a major restructuring in January, which followed years of struggles including workplace misconduct scandals, persistent difficulties getting games launched , and underperformance among big releases. Ubisoft said in today's half-year financial report report that it's reduced its headcount by roughly 1,100 people over the past six months.

Ubisoft did have a significant hit earlier this year with Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced , but that wasn't enough to prevent post-launch layoffs at developer Ubisoft Singapore. Ubisoft CEO Yves Guillemot said today that "Q2 exceeded our expectations, driven by the continued success of Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced and solid contributions from our broader portfolio."

items.title: This is technically the worst version of GTA 6 that we'll ever play
items.summary:
I've been playing GTA 6 through the morning to try to see what the fuss is about, and now I totally get it. After mere hours in the game, I'm already coming to terms with the scale of it; not just the size of the map, but the attention to detail on every object and interaction. But I have to remind myself, this is sure to be the worst version of GTA 6 we'll ever play.

That sounds like an insult, but I mean the exact opposite. If this is where the game is at launch, at its most barebones, running on years-old consoles on their way out, then think of what it will be like at its peak.

Show me the graphics menu I work for PC Gamer, so forgive my snobbery when I say the PC version should be far superior to what we're currently playing on consoles. 

A part of that is the possible frame rate bump from running on modern PC hardware. The standard PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series S/X are powered by pretty outdated architectures by today's standards: RDNA 2 and Zen 2. You're looking at the Radeon RX 6000 series and Ryzen 3000 series for PC equivalents. 

These chips have recently received support for more modern ML-powered FSR upscaling techniques from AMD, though Rockstar has only seen fit to enable FSR 4 on the Xbox Series S to help the underpowered console along. Sony also has AMD-powered upscaling tech for the PS5 Pro, but the standard PS5 doesn't get a whiff of that.

items.title: Even our bunch of diehard PC gamers aren't that bothered by 30 fps in GTA 6
items.summary:
For a bunch of performance snobs, we are a surprisingly forgiving bunch at PC Gamer. Yes, if you try to insult XCOM, you're going to get a slap, but we've only just started playing GTA 6 ( well, some of us ) and we're mostly over the whole 'only runs at 30 fps' thing already. 

It turns out, while we're happy to part with our money to buy expensive components to hit higher frame rates (and earn the right to brag about it), we're also just as happy to settle for less when a game does a lot of other things exceptionally well.

GTA 6 certainly does that. That's the impression I get from most members of the team that have played it so far. Though if Rockstar is listening, when you do get around to our precious PC version, we'd love nothing more than 4K60—maybe more.

James Bentley, Hardware Writer 

(Image credit: Future) I will no doubt appreciate frames above 100 fps when GTA 6 comes to PC. Heck, I'd even just appreciate going up to 60 fps. But in my handful of hours with the game thus far, I just have simply not been that bothered by it. Be it smart ways of masking low frames, or even just the slower, methodical control approach of the game, I'm less frustrated with my PS5 running the game at around 30 fps than I was recently playing Phantom Blade Zero at well above 40 fps on a handheld PC. 

Maybe that's down to the world having a little bit of magic to it, maybe it's the engrossing tone and atmosphere, maybe it's just because it looks so darn pretty. Maybe it's because I haven't got to the game's most hectic moments yet and haven't really needed to hit a headshot with my…

items.title: Remembering the back alley brawls of The Warriors, a Rockstar city game that isn't an open world
items.summary:
The older I get, the more fascinated I somehow become by how videogames depict night, how particular technologies at particular times give rise to particular nightlives. I've already gushed about the Starlight Zone in Sonic the Hedgehog – the mild dissociation incubated by the soft, ceaseless glare of the construction yard, the eyeless brick at the level's nadir, the sleepless glitter of the skyline. Now, let me wind the clock forward, and backward, to Rockstar Toronto's The Warriors. One long night from the late '70s, sweaty and electric and menacing, fed through dank and sullen polygons from 2005.

Probably the best move Rockstar made with their adaptation of Walter Hill's film is to retain the element of phantasmagoria. Both the game and the movie open with a view of Coney Island's Wonder Wheel, its neon lamps forming a floating tracery of Morse code, cabins swinging almost imperceptibly against solid darkness. This is a kind of night in which light is more emblem than illumination, refusing to travel far, clinging to its source like a frightened ghost.

items.title: Should you kill or spare Arnold in GTA 6?
items.summary:
Deciding whether to kill or spare Arnold in GTA 6 is the culmination of the Hey Arnold mission in Chapter 1, the 7th after you encounter Mandy during Pipework. 

Essentially, Arnold, Brian's business partner, has gone dark, so you're sent to rough him up. Arnold and his cronies will do a runner, hopping into a vehicle and speeding off. You'll need to chase them down and do a bit of high-speed shooting. This will lead to an on-foot chase, at the end of which you'll corner him on a pier, where he'll explain he wants to leave the criminal life behind and disappear. There are two choices and consequences:

Kill Arnold : Gun him down and you'll get a Hardened Criminal rating in your Criminal Profile . This is essentially GTA 6's morality system, based around how often you kill people. Obviously, killing Brian will contribute significantly towards the negative. Spare Arnold : Let him go and this will give you a Restrained rating, contributing less negatively to your Criminal Profile. Brian will also show up in a mission later if you let him live, so this seems like the best choice of the two if you want extra content. Funnily enough, if you choose neither and just wait, Arnold will leave, though this will result in the same outcome as if you decided to spare him. Besides this, there are no downsides to sparing him or advantages gained through killing him.

items.title: OLED monitor shipments have doubled from last year, and all I can say is it's well deserved
items.summary:
I feel like I say this once a week at this point, but gaming monitors occupy one of the only bright spots in the dark cloud that is PC hardware right now. They are getting better and cheaper by the day, and it seems I'm not alone in thinking this, as global OLED monitor shipments doubled in the last year. Woo, go OLED monitors.

This is according to Trendforce , which notes Asus is the market leader for global OLED monitor sales (at 21.7%), with MSI coming in second (14.5%) and Samsung coming in third (11.3%). LGE take fourth place with 8.6%, and Dell closely follows that with 8.2%. The rest of the industry has the remaining 35.7% to split among themselves.

As for total sales, Trendforce says global OLED sales got a 13% bump from last quarter to this year, and more impressively, sales for OLED monitors reportedly doubled compared to the same quarter last year. That means OLED monitors have significant upward momentum right now. 

And who can blame people for buying in? OLED monitors are known for having super vibrant colours, true blacks, and they tend to have wicked fast response times and refresh rates. The difference between IPS and OLED is so apparent when you put them beside each other, and I know, as I'm rocking a dual monitor setup with both panel technologies. 

They are a bit more expensive than IPS, and older panels can suffer from burn-in, but I can say swapping from an IPS panel to an OLED one is one of the most monumental changes I've made to my gaming setup in the last decade. Though, in fairness, that also came with a resolution bump from 1080p to 1440p.…

items.title: As GTA 6 Skips Discs, GameStop CEO Says Digital-Only 'Has Hurt Consumers' and Retailers
items.summary:
As GTA 6 launches without a physical disc, GameStop's CEO has warned that the industry's shift to digital-only games has hurt both consumers and retail.

In a well-timed shot across GTA 6's bow, GameStop boss Ryan Cohen blasted the decision to abandon physical discs as a bad move for players and his own business, as it removes a layer of ownership and the ability to re-sell games via the trade-in market — something that has historically fueled GameStop's revenue.

"When you buy a game, you should be able to sell it, trade it or lend it to a friend," Cohen told Bloomberg . "Unquestionably, the decision to move to all digital has hurt consumers, and it's also hurt GameStop." 

"Of course they don't like [trade-ins] because removing a used copy eliminates an alternative to buying new," Cohen added, without referencing any specific publisher by name. "They're taking away competition."

The decision to sell GTA 6 without a disc appears not to have dented the game's overall success. GTA 6 looks poised to shatter industry sales records — with analysts estimating preorders neared 20 million before the game went on sale — even though boxed copies include a digital download code inside only. 

Cohen's sudden defense of physical discs is somewhat ironic, as it comes just four months after he publicly dismissed physical games as meaningless to GameStop's future. Appearing on a Bloomberg podcast back in July, Cohen was asked about reports that Sony planned to phase out physical PlayStation discs by 2028. Rather than sounding the alarm for retail, Cohen brushed off the threat entirely.…

items.title: DDR6 memory modules to be almost half the size of DDR5 and almost double the max speed
items.summary:
You may not be able to buy memory right now, but the good news for a hopeful future is there's potentially quicker and smaller RAM on the horizon. JEDEC, the council that sets industry standards for RAM, has published a preview of what DDR6 could look like, and it seems like it will be itty and bitty.

According to JEDEC, DDR6 will bring with it higher bandwidth, higher capacities, better reliability, more energy efficiency, and different form factors (via VideoCardz ).

Starting with bandwidth, DDR6 RDIMMs will start at a speed of 12.8 GT/s and are set to move up to "14.4 GT/s and beyond." DDR5 maxes out at 9.2 GT/s, representing a sizable bump. It also expands the data bus from 64 to 96 DQ, which no doubt contributes to the bandwidth increase. 

That is fast, though not two times faster like DDR5 versus DDR4. It is worth noting, however, that memory modules tend to get faster over their lifetime so we don't know where that might end up.

The module for DDR6 is now 74 mm, which is almost half of the 133 mm for DDR5. This is supposedly "intended to help accommodate higher system memory density", with DDR6 supporting up to 128 GB DRAM die density (double that of DDR5). 

There are other gains to be had with DDR6 too. JEDEC says it targets an improved performance-per-watt over DDR5 "through a change to VSS-terminated IO and data-center-focused low power modes"

JEDEC says DDR6 can support a "breadth of form factors", including RDIMM, UDIMM, CAMM.

When your ride does run low on fuel, you can find a gas station on the map via the gas pump symbols:

Pull up to a pump close enough to see the prompt for "Services" Select "Refuel" (It will also display the $ cost) Press the interact button You'll see Jason or Lucia picking up the pump handle Hold down the button shown in the lower right corner to refuel When you're done, you'll see Jason or Lucia replace the pump handle You'll be back in your car Easy, right? And you'll barely have to do it since, just like real life, cars can go quite a long time without refuelling if they have a full tank, even if you're going over 60mph, which I assume you are. Note that if you steal a stranger's car, their tank may nearly be empty already.

items.title: Bank your cash in GTA 6, but always keep a few hundred on you—you never know when you'll need it

But you need to be careful with your money, especially at the start of the game when even a few hundred bucks can make or break you. While wandering around Leonida, strangers might try to rob you (big mistake), but more importantly, if you die or get arrested, you'll be penalized a few hundred dollars. There's also a $20k limit to how much you can keep on your person as you gradually accumulate more and more through play.

The solution? Stash your cash frequently. During the initial chapters of the game, you won't have a bank account, but you can store your money in your house in Key Lento by simply stashing it under the floorboards in the bedroom. This will mean you have a little money tucked away, and won't lose it when you die or get busted by the cops. .

items.title: World of Warcraft: Forever isn't mere nostalgia bait - it's rebuilding the MMO social architecture that Blizzard spent years dismantling
items.summary:
I don't play video games regularly anymore. Not because I've lost interest in them, but because I no longer make the time, the premium on which has seemed to exponentiate with age. I realised, however, in 2019 that I was a kind of sleeper agent: whenever I heard the opening notes of Legends of Azeroth , the original World of Warcraft login screen music, I would feel the reactivation of a latent part of my mind laid down when I was 10 years old. And so, like a form of possession, whenever Blizzard announces a new legacy iteration of the original WoW, no downpayment in time nor money is too great to prevent me from returning.

Here I am, then, at the launch of World of Warcraft: Forever, seven years after Blizzard first revived the original 2004 game with World of Warcraft Classic in 2019. Once more I set foot on Durotar, to spend as much time as I can levelling up a new Orc Warrior before I am forcibly unplugged by either my boss or, more likely, my wife, and so far it's been a welcome return to some of the frictional - but more involving and consequential - socialising that WoW's decades of updates had previously sanded down.

items.title: I have double-checked and yes, original 'GTA killer' Driv3r really was that rubbish
items.summary:
At this point the tragedy of Driv3r , or Driver 3, or my personal favourite Drive-thrur, is well thumbed. A familiar litany of unrealised ambition, heinous bugs, dull open-world design, and an expensive yet audibly bored voice cast, the accidental comedic highlight of which is Michelle Rodriguez flatly reeling off car theft orders from what sounds like the inside of a Michelle Rodriguez-sized tupperware container.

A more widely forgotten detail is that, for a while, there was a non-zero chance - a belief, even - that Drive Three Er was going to be the opposite. The 2003-2004 hype cycle had sowed the notion that this would in fact be the open-world crime thriller to knock Grand Theft Auto off its perch, and even 22 years before GTA 6 's idolising reviews , that was no small promise; Rockstar were still enjoying the balmy success of Vice City, and we could see San Andreas cresting the hill on a stolen, shining BMX. "Ah, but did they have Michael Madsen doing doughnuts in car parks?," publishers Atari asked the world, either unaware or in denial of the spluttering, clapped-out rattletrap they were about to wheel into the showroom.

You likely know the rest, though one of the dangers of familiarity is the subsequent breeding of complacency, which in this case can manifest as a thawing acceptance. I succumbed to this myself, having recently installed a legally unlinkable copy of Drivethreeuh, mind opened to the possibility that maybe it wasn't that bad. Six hours later, I am here to tell you: it was.

items.summary:
It's bizarre today to think of Rockstar working on games that aren't Grand Theft Auto . Frankly, it's bizarre to think of Rockstar working on games that aren't GTA 6 , which rolls onto console hard drives this week. A decade in the making, with a development team of thousands scattered across an international network of studios, GTA 6 aims to be the Maximum Game. It's both a dense, lively open world and a monument to the exhausting impersonality of "triple-A" game productions. It contains multitudes: birdlife! Realistic cloud formation! Fuel mechanics! Romance! Soda visibly sloshing around in bottles! It's an imperial production shadowed by labour disputes , that appears to have given Rockstar's various teams little time or space to think about anything else.

It wasn't ever thus. Once upon a time, Rockstar weren't just known for GTA and to a considerably lesser extent, Red Dead Redemption . Once upon a time, they had a reputation for slightly dodgy experiments. I recently interviewed former Rockstar North tech director Obbe Vermeij about a few of them, including Agent, the unofficial James Bond game Rockstar toyed with before putting all chips on Grand Theft Auto 5 .

items.title: Sony defeat $2.6 billion UK class action lawsuit which argued PlayStation's dominant market position fuels "excessive and unfair" game prices
items.summary: It's a joyous day for lawyers representing plucky little game and console makers Sony. A UK class action lawsuit which accused the company of using the PlayStation Store's dominant market position to fuel "excessive and unfair" prices for digital games has been dismissed in its entirety by the Competition Appeal Tribunal in London.
